question:
**Case Study: Linear Transformation and Symmetry in Image Processing**

An image is represented as a $2 \times 2$ grayscale matrix $P = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 200 \\ 150 & 100 \end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Apply the transpose operation to $P$ and interpret the result in the context of image reflection.
(b) Construct a new matrix $Q$ such that $P + Q$ is symmetric and $P - Q$ is skew-symmetric. Find such a $Q$.
(c) Critically analyze the value of decomposing matrices into symmetric and skew-symmetric parts in image processing, and give an example scenario where these properties are exploited.
explanation:
(a)

$P' = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 150 \\ 200 & 100 \end{bmatrix}$

Interpretation: Transposing the image matrix flips pixel values along the main diagonal—a reflection across the diagonal.

(b)

To construct $Q$: $P+Q$ symmetric, $P-Q$ skew-symmetric.

Let $S=P+Q$ (symmetric), $K=P-Q$ (skew-symmetric).

But $Q = S-P = P-K$. Thus, $Q=\frac{1}{2}(S+K)$

Alternatively, any $2\times2$ matrix $A$ can be written as $A=\frac{1}{2}(A+A') + \frac{1}{2}(A-A')$

So, $Q=\frac{1}{2}(P'+P) - \frac{1}{2}(P'-P)$

But more directly, choose $Q = P'$

Check:

$P+Q = P+P'=$
$\begin{bmatrix} 120+120 & 200+150 \\ 150+200 & 100+100 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 240 & 350 \\ 350 & 200 \end{bmatrix}$, which is symmetric.

$P-Q=P-P'=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 50 \\ -50 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, skew-symmetric (as $a_{ij} = -a_{ji}$, diagonal zero).

(c)

Decomposing into symmetric/skew-symmetric reveals structure: symmetry relates to even features/balanced contrasts; skew-symmetry, odd features or gradients. In compression, filtering, or feature detection, these properties isolate useful image aspects (e.g., edge detection exploits skew-symmetric gradients).

options.A:
(a) $P'=P$.
(b) Choose $Q=0$, so $P+Q$ is symmetric and $P-Q$ is skew-symmetric.
(c) Decomposition has no use in image processing.
options.B:
(a) $P'=\begin{bmatrix}120&150\\200&100\end{bmatrix}$, representing reflection across the main diagonal.
(b) Choose $Q=P'=\begin{bmatrix}120&150\\200&100\end{bmatrix}$; then $P+Q=\begin{bmatrix}240&350\\350&200\end{bmatrix}$ is symmetric and $P-Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&50\\-50&0\end{bmatrix}$ is skew-symmetric.
(c) Symmetric and skew-symmetric decomposition helps separate balanced image structure from directional/edge-like features.
options.C:
(a) $P'=\begin{bmatrix}100&150\\200&120\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Choose $Q=P$, so $P-Q=0$ and $P+Q$ is always skew-symmetric.
(c) It is useful only for diagonal matrices.
options.D:
(a) $P'$ is not defined because $P$ is not square.
(b) No such matrix $Q$ exists.
(c) Image matrices cannot be decomposed.
